entryPoint: SLA::isTransient() in include/class.sla.php (line ~101) — zero-argument instance method returning the bitwise-AND of $this->flags and self::FLAG_TRANSIENT (0x0008); callers use the result purely as a truthy/falsy guard.
coreLogic: Single expression, no delegation chain: `return $this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT;`. $this->flags is an int property already hydrated on the SLA ORM object (VerySimpleModel) before this method runs. No other method or class is called from within isTransient().
consumers: Ticket::transfer() in include/class.ticket.php (~line 2663): `if (!$this->getSLAId() || $this->getSLA()->isTransient()) if (($slaId=$this->getDept()->getSLAId())) $this->selectSLAId($slaId);` — when a ticket is transferred to a new department, a missing or transient current SLA triggers reselecting the SLA from the new department's default via selectSLAId(), which internally may call setSLAId()/save().

Ticket::update() in include/class.ticket.php (~line 3767): `if (!$keepSLA && (!$this->getSLA() || $this->getSLA()->isTransient())) { $this->selectSLAId(); }` — during ticket field updates, unless caller passed $keepSLA, a missing or transient SLA triggers reselection (selectSLAId() falls back through dept -> topic -> system default $cfg->getDefaultSLAId()).

Both consumers combine the isTransient() result with `!$this->getSLA()` via short-circuit boolean logic (||/&&); the return value is never stored or compared numerically, only branched on inside an `if`.
inputShape: None (zero parameters). Implicit input is the instance's own $this->flags int property (bitmask of FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0001, FLAG_ESCALATE=0x0002, FLAG_NOALERTS=0x0004, FLAG_TRANSIENT=0x0008), already loaded on the SLA object at call time.
outputShape: int — result of `$this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT`: 8 when the TRANSIENT bit is set, 0 otherwise. Every current caller treats this purely as a boolean truthy/falsy value inside `if` conditions; the raw int is never assigned, returned onward, or compared to a specific number.
sideEffects: None inside isTransient() itself: it is a pure, synchronous read of the already-loaded $this->flags property with no DB query, no global state ($cfg etc.) access, no caching, no file I/O, and no mutation of $this or any argument.

Contextual only (outside this method's scope): $this->flags is populated earlier when the SLA row is hydrated by the ORM (VerySimpleModel row load, e.g. via SLA::lookup() or Ticket's lazy 'sla' relation in getSLA()) — this hydration happens before isTransient() is ever invoked and must not be re-triggered by the extracted service.
constraints: Preserve isTransient()'s exact signature (no parameters) and exact int return semantics (0 or 8), not a coerced real boolean — no known caller depends on the specific int today, but the smallest-patch rule means we must not change the literal return value type/shape.
FLAG_TRANSIENT must remain sourced from SLA::FLAG_TRANSIENT (0x0008); the extracted service must not hardcode a duplicate constant that could drift out of sync.

Extracted service must never call back into SLA::isTransient() (anti-recursion) — it must either accept the flags int (or the SLA instance) as a parameter and reimplement the identical bitwise expression, or operate purely on data passed in from the facade.
Do not alter or extract any other SLA flag method (isActive(), sendAlerts(), hasFlag(), priorityEscalation()) or the FLAG_* constants — those are out of scope for MOD-29.
Do not modify Ticket::transfer(), Ticket::update(), or selectSLAId() in include/class.ticket.php — they are callers, not part of the seam being extracted.

Do not touch orchestrator/fixtures/MOD-25, MOD-26, MOD-27, or MOD-28, or their manifests/harnesses — new fixtures and any new harness for this ticket live only under orchestrator/fixtures/MOD-29/ and legacy/harness/ as a new file.
This is an E2E pipeline test only — resulting PR must not be merged and should be closed/deleted after the run along with any throwaway branch.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with one field: `flags` (int) — the raw SLA flags bitmask to set on a throwaway SLA instance before calling isTransient(), mirroring the existing priority_escalation_capture.php pattern (`new SLA(array('id'=>1))`, then `$sla->flags = (int) $input['flags']`, call `$sla->isTransient()`, echo `{input, output}`). Fixtures should cover: flags=0 (no bits set), FLAG_TRANSIENT only (8), FLAG_TRANSIENT combined with other bits (e.g. ACTIVE|TRANSIENT=9, ESCALATE|NOALERTS|TRANSIENT=14), all bits set (15), and a negative case with bits set but excluding TRANSIENT (e.g. ACTIVE|ESCALATE|NOALERTS=7) to prove the falsy path.
